summary: I verified the platform facts that decide this app's architecture, and two of them change the plan. First, the dataset is far smaller than assumed: all 15 OpenJLPT files (vocab+kanji+grammar, N5–N1) total 3.91 MB uncompressed (~1 MB gzipped), not "tens of MB" — so you can precache the entire corpus and skip elaborate lazy-loading, and reserve the per-level download button for the heavy stuff (baked video transcripts, pronunciation MP3s). Second, YouTube's Required Minimum Functionality terms explicitly prohibit overlays in front of an embedded player, so the "BIG subtitles over the video" design must become "video on top, big tappable dual-language subtitle panel below" — which is also better on a phone, since you can't tap a word through an overlay anyway. I also confirmed the runtime-CORS situation: jisho.org and tatoeba.org send NO Access-Control-Allow-Origin, so both are build-time-only sources; raw.githubusercontent.com does send `*`. JapanesePod101 audio works as an `<audio src>` (no CORS needed for media elements) and returns a distinctive 52288-byte placeholder when a word has no recording — that's your "audio exists" test, verified against 5 words. On the PWA side: Chrome dropped the service-worker-fetch-handler install requirement (m108 mobile), Safari's 7-day script-writable-storage eviction does NOT apply to Home Screen web apps and `navigator.storage.persist()` only grants for Home Screen apps on iOS, Wake Lock finally works in installed iOS PWAs as of iOS 18.4, and `navigator.vibrate` is still unsupported in every Safari version through 27.2 — so haptics must be progressive enhancement only. Python's `http.server` on this exact machine serves `sw.js` as `text/javascript` and `.webmanifest` as `application/manifest+json`, so local dev needs no MIME workaround.

recommendations.title: Precache the whole JLPT corpus — it is only 3.9 MB
recommendations.decision: Ship all 15 OpenJLPT JSON files (vocab+kanji+grammar N5–N1) as content-hashed files under /data/ and precache them in the service worker install step, or on first run right after the shell. Measured: vocab 3.11 MB, kanji 0.64 MB, grammar 0.05 MB = 3.91 MB total uncompressed, ~1 MB over gzip/brotli. Reserve the explicit per-level 'Download for offline' button for the genuinely heavy tier: baked YouTube transcripts, story text, and pronunciation MP3s. Show a real byte count and a progress bar on that button, driven by the SW's LEVEL_PROGRESS messages.
recommendations.why: I measured every file with curl (see verified_facts). The orchestrator's 'tens of MB' premise was wrong by an order of magnitude. Complex lazy-loading for 3.9 MB is wasted engineering and makes the app feel broken on a train; a single 1 MB download makes N5–N1 fully offline from minute one.

recommendations.title: Subtitles go BELOW the player, never on top of it
recommendations.decision: Layout: 16:9 YouTube iframe pinned at the top (sticky), then a large scrolling dual-language subtitle panel underneath that occupies the rest of the viewport. Current line in Japanese at ~clamp(26px, 7.5vw, 44px), English gloss under it at ~clamp(15px, 4.2vw, 22px). Each Japanese line is pre-segmented at build time into <button> word chips. Tapping a chip pauses the player (player.pauseVideo()), opens a bottom sheet with reading/meaning/audio, and offers 'Save'. Tapping a subtitle line seeks the player to that timestamp. Never position any element over the iframe rect.
recommendations.why: YouTube's Required Minimum Functionality page states verbatim: 'You must not display overlays, frames, or other visual elements in front of any part of a YouTube embedded player, including player controls.' An overlay would also swallow the taps you need for per-word lookup, and on a phone a 44px subtitle over a 16:9 video leaves no video visible. Minimum embed viewport is 200x200px.

recommendations.title: Bake transcripts at build time and ship a video-less 'Script Mode'
recommendations.decision: Run the verified youtubei/v1/player transcript recipe in a Node build script, store each video's timed cues as /data/video/<id>.json (with word segmentation and per-word dictionary IDs resolved at build time), and register the video page so that when navigator.onLine is false it renders the same subtitle panel with a play/pause-free 'shadowing script' reader — tap-through-lines at your own pace, word lookup fully working. Mark video entries in the UI with an 'offline: script only' badge.
recommendations.why: Browsers cannot fetch YouTube transcripts at runtime (CORS), so they must be baked anyway. Once baked, the most valuable part of the feature (tappable Japanese text with timing and English) costs zero network. Without this, the entire video section is a dead screen on the train, which is exactly the scenario the user described.

recommendations.title: jisho.org and tatoeba.org are build-time-only — plan around it
recommendations.decision: Use both in Node build scripts to enrich the shipped JSON (extra senses, JLPT-appropriate example sentences, part-of-speech tags). Do NOT call them from page JavaScript. If you want a live 'look up anything' escape hatch, the only honest options are (a) ship jmdict-eng-common as an IndexedDB-backed local dictionary, or (b) open jisho.org in a new tab. Prefer (a).
recommendations.why: Verified with curl -H 'Origin: https://example.com': neither jisho.org/api/v1/search/words nor tatoeba.org/en/api_v0/search returns any Access-Control-Allow-Origin header, so browser fetch() to them is blocked. raw.githubusercontent.com does return 'Access-Control-Allow-Origin: *', but baking is still better for offline. jmdict-eng-common is only ~1.4 MB zipped and makes lookup work offline, which is what the user actually needs.

recommendations.title: Audio: JapanesePod101 MP3 primary (baked), SpeechSynthesis as the online-only fallback
recommendations.decision: At build time, probe https://assets.languagepod101.com/dictionary/japanese/audiomp3.php?kanji=<word>&kana=<reading> for every vocab entry; treat Content-Length == 52288 as 'no recording'. Download the real ones (1.8–9 KB each) into /audio/<hash>.mp3 and ship them per level. At runtime use <audio src="/audio/..."> — no CORS needed for media elements. Where no recording exists, fall back to SpeechSynthesis with lang='ja-JP', called synchronously inside the tap handler, after resolving voices via the voiceschanged event with a 1s timeout. If neither is available, hide the speaker button rather than showing a dead one.
recommendations.why: Verified sizes: 猫/ねこ 1872 B, 水/みず 2400 B, 食べる/たべる 2760 B, 会社員/かいしゃいん 9044 B, nonsense ズズズズ 52288 B — the 52288 placeholder is a reliable sentinel. Real human audio beats TTS for pitch accent. SpeechSynthesis alone is not dependable: Android Chrome reports voices it cannot actually use and needs the Google TTS Japanese pack installed; iOS over-reports its voice list; both require user activation (Chrome since M71, Safari always); Chrome populates getVoices() asynchronously while Safari is synchronous. Bundled MP3s at ~3 KB each are the only path that works offline.

recommendations.title: Never intercept cross-origin requests in the service worker
recommendations.decision: First line of the fetch handler after the method check: `if (url.origin !== self.location.origin) return;`. Do not cache.add() any cross-origin media or API response.
recommendations.why: Cross-origin no-cors fetches produce opaque responses. Chrome pads each opaque entry in Cache Storage by roughly 7 MB against quota, so caching a few hundred 3 KB pronunciation MP3s from languagepod101 could consume gigabytes of quota and trigger eviction of the user's actual progress. Download them at build time into same-origin /audio/ instead.

recommendations.title: Handle Range requests for cached audio or Safari playback fails silently
recommendations.decision: In the SW's media route, key the cache on a Range-less Request, and when the incoming request carries a Range header, slice the cached ArrayBuffer and return a manual 206 with Content-Range / Content-Length / Accept-Ranges. Full implementation is the serveMedia() function in code_or_data.
recommendations.why: Safari's <audio> element issues Range requests. If the service worker answers a Range request with a cached 200 full-body response, Safari rejects it and the element never plays, with no console error. This is one of the most commonly hit and hardest-to-diagnose PWA audio bugs.

recommendations.title: Progress lives in IndexedDB, mirrored to localStorage, with mandatory JSON export
recommendations.decision: IndexedDB is the store of record for saved words, SRS scheduling state, and review history (structured, indexable, no 5 MB ceiling, async so it never jank-blocks a swipe). Mirror a compact snapshot into localStorage on every write as a crash/corruption backup. Call navigator.storage.persist() once on first launch AND again on every launch. Surface navigator.storage.estimate() as 'Using X MB of Y MB' in Settings. Add a big 'Back up my words' button that downloads a single nihongo-backup-YYYY-MM-DD.json (schemaVersion, savedWords, srsState, settings, reviewLog) and a matching import with a merge-or-replace choice. Nag for a backup every 30 days of use.
recommendations.why: Safari clears all script-writable storage (localStorage, IndexedDB, Cache Storage, SW registrations) after 7 days of no interaction — but Home Screen web apps have their own use counter and are exempt, and WebKit grants persist() largely on the heuristic of being a Home Screen app, which is why persist() must be re-requested each launch rather than once. WebKit also evicts by LRU under storage pressure and exempts persisted-mode origins. None of that is a guarantee, so an export file is the only thing that truly cannot be lost. Quotas themselves are generous (per-origin up to 60% of disk in a browser app, 15% for other apps; 80%/20% overall), so 3.9 MB is never the problem — eviction is.

recommendations.title: Complete install story: Android prompt + a hand-written iOS instruction sheet
recommendations.decision: Capture beforeinstallprompt, preventDefault, stash it, and show your own 'Install' button; call prompt() on tap and listen for appinstalled. Detect iOS Safari (no beforeinstallprompt, not in standalone) and show an illustrated 'Share -> Add to Home Screen' sheet instead. Detect already-installed via matchMedia('(display-mode: standalone)') OR navigator.standalone and hide both. Ship the manifest fields in code_or_data: name, short_name, start_url, scope, display + display_override, theme_color, background_color, id, launch_handler, orientation, categories, 192/512 any + 192/512 maskable icons, narrow + wide screenshots, and three shortcuts (Review / Saved / N5).
recommendations.why: Chrome removed the requirement for a service worker with a fetch handler back in m108 on mobile / m112 on desktop, so installability now hinges on HTTPS + manifest (name, icons incl. 512, start_url, display) + ~30s of user engagement; on GMS devices Chrome mints a WebAPK so it gets a real launcher entry, app switcher card and system settings row. Samsung Internet does the same on Samsung hardware. iOS has never implemented beforeinstallprompt, so without explicit instructions most users never install and then get hit by the 7-day eviction they were exempt from.

recommendations.title: iOS splash screens must be static <link> tags, one per device
recommendations.decision: Generate them with `npx pwa-asset-generator ./icons/icon.svg ./public/icons -i ./public/index.html -m ./public/manifest.webmanifest -b '#0f1115' --favicon` and paste the emitted apple-touch-startup-image links. Set apple-mobile-web-app-status-bar-style to black-translucent and then pad your header with env(safe-area-inset-top), or the iOS clock will sit on top of your UI. apple-touch-icon must be a 180x180 PNG with no transparency and no pre-rounded corners.
recommendations.why: iOS still ignores manifest-driven splash screens entirely; each startup image must match the device's exact CSS px and DPR via a media query or it is skipped, and landscape startup images are ignored (the portrait one is stretched). pwa-asset-generator 8.1.6 is current on npm and emits the whole matrix.

recommendations.title: Rely on system Japanese fonts; do not webfont-load Noto Sans JP
recommendations.decision: Font stack: `-apple-system, 'Hiragino Sans', 'Hiragino Kaku Gothic ProN', 'Noto Sans JP', 'Noto Sans CJK JP', system-ui, sans-serif`. Put lang="ja" on every element containing Japanese. Use `word-break: normal; overflow-wrap: anywhere; line-break: strict;` on Japanese blocks and `line-height: 1.8` minimum. Use native <ruby><rb>漢字<rt>かんじ</rt></ruby> for furigana with a user toggle, and set `ruby-position: over` plus explicit `rt { font-size: 0.5em; line-height: 1; }`. Reserve top padding on ruby lines (`padding-top: 0.9em`) so the reading is not clipped.
recommendations.why: Google Fonts splits Noto Sans JP into 248 unicode-range slices (verified by counting the CSS) — unusable for an offline app, and precaching all of them is multiple MB of font for zero benefit. iOS ships Hiragino Sans and Android ships Noto Sans CJK JP, so system fonts render Japanese correctly at zero bytes and zero latency. The lang="ja" attribute is load-bearing: without it Android can pick Chinese glyph variants for shared kanji when the device locale is zh. Android is known to clip <rt> at large font sizes, which the explicit padding and rt sizing work around.

recommendations.title: Mobile chrome-removal CSS: dvh, safe areas, no pull-to-refresh, no double-tap zoom
recommendations.decision: Use `height: 100dvh` (with a `100vh` line above it as fallback) for full-height screens. Set `html, body { overscroll-behavior-y: contain; }` to kill pull-to-refresh and scroll chaining, and `touch-action: manipulation` on the app root to kill the 300ms double-tap-zoom delay. On the flashcard swipe surface use `touch-action: pan-y` (or `none` if you own both axes) plus `user-select: none` and `-webkit-touch-callout: none`. Pad the layout with `padding: env(safe-area-inset-top) env(safe-area-inset-right) env(safe-area-inset-bottom) env(safe-area-inset-left)` and keep every tap target >= 48x48 CSS px with >= 8px gaps. Do NOT set user-scalable=no — it is an accessibility failure and ignored by iOS anyway.
recommendations.why: overscroll-behavior is Baseline since Safari 16 (2022) and is the native, non-hacky replacement for preventDefault()-ing touchmove, which breaks scrolling. touch-action: manipulation is the correct double-tap-zoom fix. env() insets only resolve to non-zero when the viewport meta includes viewport-fit=cover. 100dvh is the fix for the iOS 100vh-under-the-toolbar bug.

recommendations.title: Wake Lock during video and review, with a visibilitychange re-acquire
recommendations.decision: Request navigator.wakeLock.request('screen') when the video player or a timed review session starts, release it on pause/exit, and re-request it inside a visibilitychange handler when document.visibilityState returns to 'visible' (the lock is dropped automatically when the tab is hidden). Wrap it in a feature check and try/catch — never let a rejection break playback.
recommendations.why: Screen Wake Lock is supported in Safari from iOS 16.4, but a long-standing bug broke it specifically inside installed PWAs until Apple fixed it in iOS 18.4 (March 2025). As of 2026 it is above 94% global support across Chromium, Firefox and Safari on desktop, Android, iPadOS and iOS. The re-acquire is required by spec, not optional.

recommendations.title: Haptics are Android-only — design so their absence is invisible
recommendations.decision: Wrap every call as `navigator.vibrate?.(10)` and use it only for confirmation flourishes (card flip 8ms, correct answer 12ms, wrong answer [20,40,20]). Always pair it with a visual and/or audio cue so iOS users lose nothing. Never gate feedback on vibration succeeding.
recommendations.why: caniuse shows Safari does not support the Vibration API in any version from 3.2 through 27.2, and Firefox dropped it at 129+. Global support is 79%, entirely from Chromium/Android. If a flashcard's only 'correct!' signal is a buzz, half the users get silence.

recommendations.title: Use FSRS, not SM-2, for the flashcard scheduler
recommendations.decision: Implement FSRS. Vendor ts-fsrs 5.4.2 (dist/index.mjs is 61 KB, served by jsDelivr, ESM, no build step needed — copy it into /vendor/ts-fsrs.mjs and import it directly). Store per-card {due, stability, difficulty, elapsed_days, scheduled_days, reps, lapses, state, last_review} in IndexedDB. Expose the standard four buttons (Again / Hard / Good / Easy) as big thumb-reachable targets at the bottom of the card, plus swipe-left = Again and swipe-right = Good for one-handed speed.
recommendations.why: Benchmarks over 500M+ Anki reviews show FSRS needs 20–30% fewer reviews than SM-2 for the same retention; it has been the state of the art since Anki 23.10 adopted it, and for a user whose stated goal is 'learn basic Japanese fast' that is a direct 20–30% time saving. ts-fsrs 5.4.2 is current on npm and I confirmed cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/ts-fsrs@5.4.2/dist/index.mjs returns HTTP 200, 61245 bytes.

recommendations.title: Cache versioning that cannot break a running session
recommendations.decision: Three caches: shell-<BUILD> (replaced wholesale per deploy), data-v1 (content-hashed immutable level files, cache-first and never revalidated), media-v1 (same-origin audio, LRU-trimmed). Do NOT call skipWaiting() in install. Let the new worker wait, detect it from the page via registration.onupdatefound + installingWorker.state === 'installed' && navigator.serviceWorker.controller, show a non-blocking 'Update ready — tap to restart' bar, and only then postMessage({type:'SKIP_WAITING'}) and reload on controllerchange (guarded against reload loops). Enable navigationPreload in activate. Precache shell URLs individually in a try/catch loop, not via one addAll().
recommendations.why: skipWaiting() mid-session swaps the SW under a page whose JS expects the old asset graph, which is exactly how a flashcard review gets destroyed halfway through. Content-hashed data URLs mean the data cache never needs invalidation — new build, new filename, old entries dropped by the cleanup in activate. addAll() is all-or-nothing: one 404 on a screenshot silently aborts the entire install and the app is never offline-capable.

recommendations.title: Serving and hosting: exact commands for this machine
recommendations.decision: Desktop dev: `cd <project> && python -m http.server 8080` then http://localhost:8080 (localhost is a secure context, so SW + install work). Phone on the same wifi: http://192.168.10.110:8080 will render but the service worker will NOT register, because a LAN IP over plain HTTP is not a secure context. Two fixes: (a) Android via USB — chrome://inspect > Port forwarding > 8080 -> localhost:8080, then open http://localhost:8080 on the phone, which IS a secure context; (b) any phone incl. iPhone — `npx localtunnel --port 8080` or `npx cloudflared tunnel --url http://localhost:8080` gives a real HTTPS URL. Permanent free hosting (git is installed at C:\Program Files\Git): GitHub Pages via a gh-pages branch, or `npx wrangler@4 pages deploy ./public --project-name nihongo-ladder` for Cloudflare Pages. Both give HTTPS, which PWA install requires.
recommendations.why: I confirmed the LAN IPv4 is 192.168.10.110 and that python -m http.server 8080 on this machine serves sw.js as 'text/javascript' and manifest.webmanifest as 'application/manifest+json' (a wrong .js MIME type is a classic Windows registry gotcha that silently kills SW registration — this machine is clean, so no workaround needed). localtunnel 2.0.2, cloudflared 0.7.3 and wrangler 4.135.0 are all live on npm. Service workers are hard-restricted to secure contexts, localhost excepted.

recommendations.title: Set manifest orientation to "any", not "portrait"
recommendations.decision: Ship "orientation": "any" and control layout with CSS media queries: portrait for study screens, and let the video screen reflow (or go fullscreen via the YouTube player's own control) in landscape.
recommendations.why: On Android a WebAPK honours the manifest orientation for the whole app. Locking to portrait would make landscape video — the one place a phone user genuinely wants landscape — impossible. Screen Orientation lock API is unsupported on iOS anyway, so CSS is the only cross-platform lever.

recommendations.title: Extra features the research says actually move the needle
recommendations.decision: Add, in rough priority order: (1) a daily goal + streak with a due-count badge, driven from the FSRS queue; (2) kanji drill-down from any vocab word (OpenJLPT kanji JSON has onyomi/kunyomi/strokes/freq — 2,211 entries, 0.64 MB total); (3) a furigana on/off toggle wired to the ruby elements; (4) romaji input for search via vendored wanakana 5.3.1; (5) a 'Business & Workplace Japanese' track that is a separate tag layer over N3–N1 vocab (keigo: 尊敬語/謙譲語/丁寧語 patterns, email templates, 報連相, meeting phrases, 名刺交換) rather than a sixth level — this is the user's stated endgame and no JLPT dataset covers it, so it has to be authored; (6) an 'export saved words to Anki CSV' button (expression,reading,meaning,tags) matching the open-anki-jlpt-decks column layout so the user is never locked in; (7) a shuffle/quiz mode (JP->EN and EN->JP multiple choice) for variety between SRS sessions.
recommendations.why: The user asked for 'anything helpful' and named a basic-to-professional arc. Business Japanese is the one requirement no verified dataset supplies, so flagging it early prevents a late surprise. The Anki export is cheap insurance against the eviction risk and matches a format already proven by jamsinclair/open-anki-jlpt-decks. Streaks and due-counts are the standard retention mechanic in every successful SRS app and fall out of the FSRS state you are already storing.

verified_facts.claim: The full OpenJLPT dataset (vocab+kanji+grammar, N5-N1) is only 3.91 MB uncompressed, not tens of MB

verified_facts.evidence: curl -sI -H 'Origin: https://example.com' 'https://tatoeba.org/en/api_v0/search?from=jpn&to=eng&query=食べる&limit=2' -> 'HTTP/1.1 200 OK', 'Content-Type: application/json', no access-control-allow-origin header.

verified_facts.claim: raw.githubusercontent.com DOES send Access-Control-Allow-Origin: *, so runtime fetch of the OpenJLPT files would work
verified_facts.evidence: curl -sI -H 'Origin: https://example.com' on the n5 vocab URL returned 'HTTP/1.1 200 OK', 'Access-Control-Allow-Origin: *', 'Content-Type: text/plain; charset=utf-8'.

verified_facts.claim: JapanesePod101 audio endpoint works and returns a 52288-byte placeholder file for words with no recording
verified_facts.evidence: Probed 5 words via curl -sL -o /dev/null -w '%{size_download}': 猫/ねこ -> 1872 B; 水/みず -> 2400 B; 食べる/たべる -> 2760 B; 会社員/かいしゃいん -> 9044 B; nonsense ズズズズ/ずずずず -> exactly 52288 B. Content-Type: audio/mpeg, HTTP 200 in all cases (via one 301 redirect). No access-control-allow-origin header, which is fine for <audio src> but means it cannot be fetch()ed or safely Cache-API'd.

verified_facts.claim: YouTube's terms explicitly prohibit overlaying anything in front of an embedded player
verified_facts.evidence: developers.google.com/youtube/terms/required-minimum-functionality, verbatim: 'You must not display overlays, frames, or other visual elements in front of any part of a YouTube embedded player, including player controls.' and 'you must not use overlays, frames or other visual elements to obscure any part of an embedded player, including player controls.' Minimum embed viewport stated as 200px by 200px; 16:9 recommended at >= 480x270.

verified_facts.claim: Chrome no longer requires a service worker with a fetch handler for installability
verified_facts.evidence: developer.chrome.com/blog/update-install-criteria: 'we have removed the requirement to have a service worker that implements the fetch() method for installation from the menu, since version 108 on mobile and 112 on Desktop.' Still strongly recommends short_name/name, icons (maskable preferred), start_url and display.

verified_facts.claim: Safari's 7-day script-writable storage eviction does not apply to Home Screen web apps, and persist() is granted on iOS mainly via the Home-Screen-app heuristic
verified_facts.evidence: webkit.org/blog/14403/updates-to-storage-policy/ documents LRU eviction with exemptions for origins that have an active page or storage in persistent mode (StorageManager.persist()), and per-origin quota up to 60% of disk for browser apps / 15% for other apps, overall 80% / 20%. Search corroboration: home screen web apps keep their own days-of-use counter that resets on use; WebKit grants persistent storage 'based on heuristics like whether the website is opened as a Home Screen Web App', and the permission must be re-requested each launch.

verified_facts.claim: Screen Wake Lock works in installed iOS PWAs only from iOS 18.4 onward
verified_facts.evidence: Supported in Safari from iOS 16.4, but a long-standing bug broke the API specifically inside installed PWAs until Apple fixed it in iOS 18.4 (released 2025-03-31). As of 2026, >94% global support across Chromium, Firefox and Safari on desktop, Android, iPadOS and iOS (web.dev, caniuse, web-platform-dx features explorer).

verified_facts.claim: navigator.vibrate is unsupported in every version of Safari, desktop and iOS
verified_facts.evidence: caniuse.com/vibration: 'Safari on iOS versions 3.2 through 27.2 do not support the Vibration API.' Global support 79.28%; supported in Chrome 30+, Edge 79+, Chrome for Android, Samsung Internet 4+; Firefox dropped it at 129+.

verified_facts.claim: iOS still ignores manifest splash screens; they must be static apple-touch-startup-image links sized per device
verified_facts.evidence: Multiple sources incl. web.dev/learn/pwa/enhancements and Apple developer forums: startup images must be declared in HTML with rel='apple-touch-startup-image', must match the exact window size of the PWA on that device via a media query, need one image per device, and landscape variants are ignored (Safari stretches the portrait one).

verified_facts.claim: python -m http.server on this machine serves correct MIME types for PWA files (no Windows registry MIME bug)
verified_facts.evidence: Started `python -m http.server 8731` in the scratchpad and curl -sI each file: sw.js -> 'Content-type: text/javascript'; manifest.webmanifest -> 'Content-type: application/manifest+json'; index.html -> 'Content-type: text/html'. Python 3.13.14 mimetypes.guess_type also returns text/javascript for .js and .mjs, application/manifest+json for .webmanifest.

verified_facts.claim: ts-fsrs 5.4.2 is available as a ready-to-vendor ESM file requiring no build step
verified_facts.evidence: registry.npmjs.org shows dist-tags.latest = 5.4.2. curl -o /dev/null -w '%{http_code} %{size_download}' on https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/ts-fsrs@5.4.2/dist/index.mjs returned '200 61245'. jsDelivr package listing also shows index.umd.js (72,009 B) and index.cjs (62,470 B).

verified_facts.claim: Google Fonts serves Noto Sans JP as 248 unicode-range slices, making it impractical for an offline PWA
verified_facts.evidence: curl of https://fonts.googleapis.com/css2?family=Noto+Sans+JP:wght@400;700&display=swap with a Chrome UA, then `grep -c unicode-range` -> 248.

verified_facts.claim: This machine's LAN address is 192.168.10.110 and the required tooling is present
verified_facts.evidence: ipconfig -> 'IPv4 Address . . . : 192.168.10.110'. node v24.18.0, npx 11.16.0, Python 3.13.14, git at C:\Program Files\Git\cmd\git.exe. cloudflared and ngrok are NOT installed locally, but npm has cloudflared@0.7.3, localtunnel@2.0.2 and wrangler@4.135.0. fonttools is NOT installed (needed only if you decide to subset a Japanese webfont).

verified_facts.claim: pwa-asset-generator is current and can emit the whole iOS icon/splash matrix
verified_facts.evidence: registry.npmjs.org/pwa-asset-generator -> dist-tags.latest = 8.1.6. (sharp 0.35.4 also available if you prefer to generate icons yourself in Node.)

risks: Do NOT overlay subtitles on the YouTube player. YouTube's Required Minimum Functionality terms prohibit it verbatim ('You must not display overlays, frames, or other visual elements in front of any part of a YouTube embedded player, including player controls'), and an overlay would also intercept the taps the per-word lookup depends on. Put the player on top and the big subtitle panel below it.

Do NOT call jisho.org or tatoeba.org from page JavaScript. I verified neither returns an Access-Control-Allow-Origin header, so every browser fetch() will fail with a CORS error even though curl works fine. They are build-time sources only. Testing with curl and assuming the browser will behave the same is the single easiest way to lose a day here.

Do NOT let the service worker cache cross-origin responses. Chrome pads each opaque Cache Storage entry by roughly 7 MB against the origin quota, so caching a few hundred 3 KB pronunciation MP3s could blow past gigabytes and trigger eviction of the user's saved words. The `if (url.origin !== self.location.origin) return;` guard must be the first thing in the fetch handler.

Do NOT return a cached 200 full-body response to a Range request. Safari's <audio> element sends Range headers and silently refuses to play a 200 — no console error, no event, just nothing. The serveMedia() 206-slicing path is mandatory, not optional.

Do NOT call skipWaiting() inside install. It swaps the service worker under a live page, which will destroy a flashcard review in progress. Let the worker wait and gate the swap behind a user-tapped 'Restart'. Also guard the controllerchange reload with a boolean or you get an infinite reload loop.

Do NOT precache with a single cache.addAll(). It is all-or-nothing: one 404 on a screenshot or a renamed icon aborts the entire install, the SW never activates, and the app is silently never offline-capable. Add each URL in its own try/catch.

Do NOT assume the user will install on iOS. Safari has never implemented beforeinstallprompt, so with no explicit 'Share > Add to Home Screen' sheet most users stay in the browser tab — where Safari wipes IndexedDB, localStorage, Cache Storage and the SW registration after 7 days of no interaction. The Home Screen exemption is the entire reason installing matters for this app, and it is also the heuristic WebKit uses to grant navigator.storage.persist().
Do NOT call navigator.storage.persist() only once at first run. On iOS the grant depends on the Home-Screen-app heuristic, which changes the moment the user installs; re-request it on every launch.

Do NOT make any feedback depend on navigator.vibrate. caniuse confirms Safari has never supported the Vibration API in any version through 27.2 (79% global support, all Chromium/Android). Pair every haptic with a visual cue.

Do NOT ship a Japanese webfont. Google Fonts splits Noto Sans JP into 248 unicode-range slices (I counted them) — precaching that for offline is multiple MB and hundreds of entries for zero benefit over the Hiragino/Noto CJK fonts already on every iOS and Android device.
Do NOT omit lang="ja" on Japanese text. Without it, Android devices set to a Chinese locale render shared kanji with Chinese glyph variants, which quietly teaches the user wrong stroke shapes.

Do NOT omit viewport-fit=cover. Without it env(safe-area-inset-*) resolves to 0px and your header sits under the iPhone notch and the iOS clock — especially with apple-mobile-web-app-status-bar-style=black-translucent, which is what makes the app look native in the first place.

Do NOT deploy to a GitHub Pages project site (github.io/repo-name/) without rewriting start_url, scope, id and every absolute path in sw.js to /repo-name/. The SW scope will not cover the app and nothing will work offline. Prefer Cloudflare Pages or a custom domain.

Do NOT change the manifest "id" after first release. Chrome treats a changed id as an entirely different app: the existing WebAPK is orphaned and the user's install (and the storage-persistence heuristics tied to it) is lost.
Do NOT lock manifest orientation to "portrait". On Android WebAPKs honour it app-wide, which makes landscape video impossible — the one place a phone user actually wants landscape.
Do NOT expect background sync or reliable background anything on iOS; there is none. Every data operation must complete while the app is in the foreground.

Do NOT rely on SpeechSynthesis as the primary pronunciation source. Android Chrome enumerates Japanese voices it cannot actually use unless the Google TTS Japanese pack is installed, iOS over-reports its voice list, both require user activation, and none of it works offline. Bundled MP3s are the only offline-safe path.

The OpenJLPT grammar data is only ~20 points per level (9-10 KB per file) against a real JLPT requirement of roughly 80-200 per level. Treat the grammar section as needing an authored or supplementary source, and be explicit in the UI about coverage rather than presenting 20 points as complete.

Business/workplace Japanese — the user's stated endgame — is not covered by any verified dataset. It must be authored as a tag layer over N3-N1 vocabulary (keigo registers, email templates, meeting and phone phrases). Plan for that content work rather than discovering the gap after the N5-N1 pipeline is done.
